skill.name: performance-analyzer
skill.description: Analyze influencer campaign performance across reach, engagement, creators, platforms, content formats, sentiment, and conversions. It turns supplied campaign data into scorecards, rankings, attribution notes, and clear optimization recommendations.
skill.summary: Analyze influencer campaign results and identify what to renew, change, or test next.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown links, code fences, placeholders, and influencer handle examples. One documented connector command is a real external-command risk, and its use of YOUTUBE_API_KEY is a real environment-access risk, but I found no malicious intent or prompt injection.

remediation.issue: The YouTube connector command executes python3 from the skill documentation.
remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before running the connector, and show the exact command and data source before execution.

remediation.issue: The YouTube connector relies on YOUTUBE_API_KEY from the environment.
remediation.suggestion: Document that the key is only used for YouTube API reads and must never be logged, saved, or included in reports.

content.value_statement: Influencer reports often mix platform metrics, creator claims, and sales data without clear decisions. This skill organizes the data into scorecards, rankings, attribution notes, and next-step recommendations.
actual_capabilities: Builds campaign scorecards against targets and benchmarks.
Ranks platforms, influencers, and content formats by performance.
Reviews engagement quality, comment sentiment, and purchase intent signals.
Breaks down conversions by promo code, UTM, direct, or estimated attribution.
Produces ranked learnings and recommendations for renewals or future tests.
Can use a documented YouTube connector for measured public video metrics when approved.
limitations: Requires campaign metrics, exports, screenshots, or pasted data from the user.
Does not calculate full dollar-level ROI; it hands inputs to an ROI skill.
Cannot verify private platform data without supplied reports or approved connectors.
Statistical winner claims depend on sufficient sample size and benchmark quality.

use_cases.title: Review a completed influencer campaign
use_cases.description: Turn post-campaign reach, engagement, conversion, and revenue data into an executive-ready performance analysis.

use_cases.title: Compare creators before renewal decisions
use_cases.description: Rank creators by performance and explain which partnerships to renew, expand, reduce, or stop.

use_cases.title: Find content patterns for the next campaign
use_cases.description: Identify the formats, hooks, messages, and platforms that produced the strongest results.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze one campaign
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with campaign data ready.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze performance for this influencer campaign. I will provide the campaign dates, creators, platforms, targets, and available metrics.

prompt_templates.title: Compare creator results
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request focused on renewal choices.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these influencers from one campaign and rank them by reach, engagement quality, conversions, and renewal recommendation.

prompt_templates.title: Explain platform and content performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze which platforms, formats, hooks, and messages performed best. Separate strong evidence from early signals that need more testing.

prompt_templates.title: Build a full performance readout
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request with multiple data sources.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a full influencer performance readout using platform exports, creator reports, web analytics, promo codes, targets, and benchmarks. Include attribution limits and next actions.

output_examples.input: Analyze our summer skincare campaign with ten creators across TikTok and Instagram.
output_examples.output: A scorecard showing reach, engagement, conversions, revenue, top creators, underperformers, key content patterns, and renewal recommendations.

output_examples.input: Compare these three creators and tell me who to renew.
output_examples.output: A ranked creator comparison with performance reasons, confidence notes, engagement quality signals, and renew or replace guidance.

output_examples.input: Find what content worked best in this campaign.
output_examples.output: A content analysis naming the strongest formats, hooks, platforms, sentiment themes, and experiments to repeat in the next campaign.

best_practices: Provide targets, date ranges, platform metrics, and conversion data before asking for final recommendations.
Label each metric source as measured, user-provided, or estimated.
Use significance checks before treating a creator, platform, or format as a proven winner.
anti_patterns: Do not claim ROI precision when only engagement data is available.
Do not compare creators without normalizing by spend, content count, or audience size.
Do not treat private platform screenshots and API metrics as identical sources.

faq.question: What data should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide campaign dates, creator handles, platform metrics, targets, benchmarks, web analytics, sales data, and promo-code results when available.

faq.question: Can it calculate ROI?
faq.answer: It can prepare performance and conversion inputs, but detailed ROI math belongs in the related ROI calculator skill.

faq.question: Does it need live platform access?
faq.answer: No. It works with pasted data, exports, and screenshots. A documented YouTube connector is optional when approved.

faq.question: Can it compare influencers fairly?
faq.answer: Yes, when you provide enough data to normalize results by spend, audience size, content volume, and campaign objective.

faq.question: Will it identify winning content patterns?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare formats, themes, hooks, messages, sentiment, and conversion signals across campaign content.

faq.question: How does it handle uncertain data?
faq.answer: It should label estimates clearly, separate measured data from supplied data, and mark weak signals as keep-testing.
